workflow.decision: When an input contract is unclear, use changes in diagnostics to identify the next unresolved format or argument question and consult the relevant standard. Treat the resulting contract model as provisional; diagnostic progress alone does not establish successful behavior.

When callable selection is undocumented, constrain candidate hypotheses using known receiver and runtime conventions rather than arbitrary guessing. The remaining question is which candidates actually belong to the installed interface and its intended contract.

When a result is absent at observation time, distinguish operation failure from a result that may have existed and then been cleaned up. A late negative observation leaves the creation, cleanup, and observation order unresolved.

tools.purpose: Locate the stated request-format standard instead of continuing to guess the format.
tools.when: A changed diagnostic suggests a recognizable documented request protocol.

handoffs.when: Diagnostics suggest input-selected behavior, but the receiving object, argument contract, and intended selectable set remain unresolved.
packet: one unresolved dispatch-contract question and contrasting predictions
diagnostic observations with provenance and author-report versus independently observed classification
candidate-selection rationale and supporting runtime or protocol documentation
receiving-object and argument-binding model with inferred edges marked
known permitted-operation control, unknown gates, and a bounded benign validation proposal
handoffs.acceptance_gate: The consumer can separate documented conventions and diagnostic inferences from confirmed dispatch. Missing receiver, actor, or binding evidence remains an explicit question; a changed error is not accepted as proof of unintended execution.

limitations: This is a historical, challenge-specific configuration, not evidence of current software behavior. All target behavior and outcomes remain source-author reports; no target requests or local reproduction were performed.
Several diagnostics and outcomes appear in screenshots. Extraction used the surrounding prose; screenshot contents and detailed error contracts were not independently decoded or verified.

The author presents periodic cleanup as a tentative configuration explanation. Its mechanism and timing were not independently measured, so the retained lesson concerns observation ambiguity rather than an established lifecycle defect or race.

Runtime conventions provide candidate hypotheses, not proof of callable reachability, authorization, or impact. The article does not supply systematic negative controls or comprehensive interface coverage.
No remediation or shipped-fix evidence is provided. Proposed validation and handoff gates are library synthesis, not claims that the author followed those contracts.

candidate_additions.guidance: Treat successive diagnostics as a provisional input-contract model. Compare them with relevant standards, record the inferred validation or binding stage, and retain the next unresolved question instead of equating a changed error with successful execution.

For undocumented behavior selectors, justify a small candidate set from receiver and runtime conventions rather than guessing arbitrary names. Keep convention-derived candidates separate from the intended allowed set and from confirmed reachability.

Before interpreting an absent transient result as operation failure, account for observation latency and possible cleanup. Preserve evidence of creation, removal, and observation ordering where available; otherwise classify the late negative result as inconclusive rather than disproving the operation.
